_comment: Jobs that have run at least once and have NEVER succeeded, which are ALREADY KNOWN and
are blocked on something outside CI. Being on this list downgrades a job from a hard
failure to a reported exception. It does NOT make it fine.
THIS LIST MAY ONLY SHRINK. The audit fails if a job that has never succeeded is absent
from it (an unacknowledged never-successful job), AND it fails if a job on the list has
since succeeded (a stale entry that must be deleted). Both directions are enforced, so
the list cannot quietly become a place where failures go to be forgotten.
Why this check exists at all: public.cron_job_health(N) judges liveness inside an N-hour
window. A weekly job runs once every 168 hours, so for six days in seven its window
contains no runs at all, failures_in_window is 0, and the verdict is 'healthy'. Measured
2026-08-24: sync-award-rates-weekly had exactly one lifetime run, it FAILED, and the
audit reported it healthy. A window-relative verdict structurally cannot see a failure
of any job whose period exceeds the window. This check is window-independent.

jobs.reason: vault entries document_retention_sweep_url and document_retention_sweep_secret were never seeded; migration 20260822080000 created the job but the secrets need real values.
jobs.blocked_on: operator — vault.create_secret() needs the actual endpoint URL and token
jobs.impact: Document retention is a compliance obligation and has never once executed.

jobs.reason: vault entries sync_award_rates_url and sync_award_rates_token were never seeded. The job refuses to POST to a null endpoint rather than reporting a false success, which is correct behaviour.
jobs.blocked_on: operator — same vault seeding, and B-2 (the FAIRWORK_API_KEY repository secret) upstream of it
jobs.impact: Award rates are never refreshed from source; every rate quoted is a bundled snapshot with no provenance stamp.
